comments.body:
## This defect has a second instance, and it does not have the same fix

Investigating four ALARM-state `rebar/host` alarms on 2026-09-06 (`rebar-container-reaper-not-active`,
`rebar-var-tmp-cleanup-not-active`, `rebar-container-writable-usage-high`, `rebar-var-tmp-usage-high`)
led back to exactly this mechanism, but on the OTHER TWO cap scripts. Filed as
`exorable-gemstone-bluefish` (`1e63-bee1-5ce6-4d8f`) and closed as a duplicate of this ticket; its
evidence is folded in here.

`observability.sh` resolves four cap scripts as siblings of the running probe, not two:

```
 458: DOCKER_CAP_SH=...   /docker-storage-cap.sh
 925: JOURNALD_CAP_SH=... /journald-cap.sh
 999: VARTMP_CAP_SH=...   /vartmp-cap.sh
1092: CONTAINER_CAP_SH=... /container-cap.sh
```

The first two were repaired by the manual copy this ticket records (they are on the host dated
`Sep 5 01:05`, and `docker_storage_used_percent` / `journal_used_percent` publish normally).
**The second two were never placed at all**, so the same failure is still live:

```
bash: /usr/local/bin/vartmp-cap.sh: No such file or directory     rc=127
bash: /usr/local/bin/container-cap.sh: No such file or directory  rc=127
```

Consequences, matching this ticket's two consequence classes exactly:
- gated percent metrics silent: `var_tmp_used_percent` and `container_writable_used_percent` are
  absent from the namespace entirely (0 datapoints in 3h; not in `list-metrics`).
- ungated heartbeats pinned to a false 0: `var_tmp_cleanup_active` and `container_reaper_active`
  publish 0 because `--check-active` returns empty and `case` coerces it — the same
  `journal_cap_in_effect` failure shape described in this ticket's consequence 2, on two more metrics.

## The part that changes AC1

For `docker-storage-cap.sh` / `journald-cap.sh`, "deploy every script the probe resolves" is
sufficient — neither defines an installed path, so their repo basename is the only name they have.

**`vartmp-cap.sh` and `container-cap.sh` are different: they self-install under a different name.**

```
infra/scripts/vartmp-cap.sh:121    VAR_TMP_INSTALLED_PATH="${...:-/usr/local/bin/rebar-vartmp-cap.sh}"
infra/scripts/container-cap.sh:124 CONTAINER_INSTALLED_PATH="${...:-/usr/local/bin/rebar-container-cap.sh}"
```

Their `--install` writes the `rebar-`-prefixed name (it is the `ExecStart` the reaper units point
at). So satisfying AC1 by the installer direction alone would place a SECOND copy at the unprefixed
name, and the box would carry two copies of the same script — the probe reading one, the reaper
timer executing the other, free to drift on the next partial deploy. For these two the
resolver direction is the one that composes; picking the first existing candidate from an ordered
list (installed name, then repo-sibling name) leaves exactly one copy on the host.

## Proven, not inferred: repairing the host does NOT repair the metric

With operator-authorised `vartmp-cap.sh --install` and `container-cap.sh --install` run on
i-00880b2c7f13527c5 at 2026-09-06 01:23Z (both rc=0; `rebar-var-tmp-reaper.timer` and
`rebar-container-reaper.timer` now in force), the truth and what the probe can see disagree:

```
# truth, via the installed prefixed path
vartmp_true=[1]      container_true=[1]
# what the probe actually calls
bash: /usr/local/bin/vartmp-cap.sh: No such file or directory
bash: /usr/local/bin/container-cap.sh: No such file or directory
```

So a host with both reapers correctly installed still publishes `0` for both heartbeats and still
omits both percentages. That isolates this ticket's defect from the host's configuration state:
the two dead-man alarms will keep firing on a now-healthy host until the resolution is fixed, which
is the `journal_cap_in_effect` "false 0 forever" failure reproducing on two more metrics.

## What the alarms were hiding

`/var/tmp` measured 3664 MiB against the 4 GiB budget `--print-env` reports — about **89%**, over
the 85% threshold of `rebar-var-tmp-usage-high`, and all 317,710 files were older than 7 days
(2.85 GB of `rebar-review-rehearsal.*` scratch). `/etc/tmpfiles.d/99-rebar-var-tmp.conf` did not
exist. The alarms were correct and unfalsifiable at the same time.

## Ruled out

Not probe staleness and not truncation: `sha256(/usr/local/bin/rebar-observability.sh)` equals
`sha256(origin/main infra/scripts/observability.sh)` = `6d900dbde913...`, so `aaa31f11f3bc` (the
probe time-budget fix) IS deployed, and `probe_ok` / `probe_truncated` publish normally. No
`terraform apply` is implicated either: all four alarms are already live in AWS from
`monitoring_autodeploy.tf` with the config the code expects (`breaching`, 6/6).

Existing tests cannot catch any of this: `tests/scripts/test_observability_*.py` run
`infra/scripts/observability.sh` in place, where every cap script IS a sibling. The suite exercises
the checkout layout and never the installed layout.

comments.body:
## Change 2722 pushed — AC1/AC2/AC4/AC5/AC6/AC7 implemented, AC3 NOT

https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2722 "Let the probe reach the cap scripts it runs"
(`ace7d9aa18de`).

**What it does.** `observability.sh` gains `resolve_cap_sh`, an ordered candidate lookup used by
the two self-installing cap scripts; the sibling is tried FIRST so the change is strictly
additive and the checkout layout every existing suite drives is untouched, with the
`*_INSTALLED_PATH` name reached only when the sibling is absent. `install-observability.sh` now
deploys `docker-storage-cap.sh` and `journald-cap.sh` beside the probe — the two whose repo
basename is the only name they have. `vartmp-cap.sh` / `container-cap.sh` are deliberately NOT
installed there, so exactly one copy of each remains on the box (AC5).

**Tests.** `tests/scripts/test_observability_cap_deps.py` (new) derives the cap set from the
probe's own text and asserts per script that the strategy covering it matches how it installs, so
renaming an installed path or dropping a script from the installer fails the build (AC2/AC4); a
discovery test guards the derivation against a regex that stops matching and passes vacuously.
Both metric suites gain an end-to-end installed-layout case. All three are defect-seeded and
were confirmed RED against the old code — the var_tmp one fails with `expected exactly one
var_tmp_used_percent datapoint, got []`, the production symptom exactly.

`make lint` and `make typecheck` clean; 119 tests across the seven affected `tests/scripts/`
suites pass (AC7).

## AC3 is NOT implemented — deliberately, and it needs a decision

The heartbeats still publish `0` rather than distinguishing "not in force" from "could not
determine". Once the resolution is fixed the input is reachable, so the false 0 does not arise
from THIS cause any more — but the coercion is still there for the next path that breaks
differently.

It was left out because it is not a local edit: bug `herbal-garish-monkey`
(`bff5-9163-cddd-4158`) deliberately requires every `rebar/host` heartbeat to publish on EVERY
tick INCLUDING its 0 path, precisely so absence means "the probe or host is dead". AC3's
"publish silence instead" is in direct tension with that, and the alarms are
`treat_missing_data = "breaching"` at 6/6, so silence still pages — the two designs page
identically and differ only in what the operator reads. Resolving that is a design decision
about which signal wins, not a fix to slip into a resolution change, and it should be argued
against `bff5` rather than around it.

## Host state, for the record

Operator-authorised `vartmp-cap.sh --install` and `container-cap.sh --install` were run at
2026-09-06 01:23Z (both rc=0). `/etc/tmpfiles.d/99-rebar-var-tmp.conf` and both reaper timers now
exist where none did before. Measured effect: `/var/tmp` 3664 MiB -> 1 MiB (3.6 GiB of
`rebar-review-rehearsal.*` scratch, every file older than 7 days), root disk 75% -> 70%. Both
timers survived the later reboot and are firing on their 5-minute period.

The four alarms remain in ALARM and should stay there until 2722 lands and autodeploy
re-materializes the probe. **No alarm was retuned, and none should be**: two are firing on
conditions that were true, and the other two are dead-man firings whose publisher this change
repairs.

comments.body:
## AC3 IS implemented after all — as a sentinel, not as silence

Superseding my previous comment's deferral. Patchset 2 of
https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2722 (`98bbafdad1d3`, same Change-Id) implements
AC3's intent without contradicting `herbal-garish-monkey` (`bff5-9163-cddd-4158`).

**The defect was the COERCION, not the publishing.** `--check-active` returning empty is
*unknown*; `case "$x" in 1) ;; *) x=0` asserted *not active*. Those are different claims, and an
operator reading `0` could not tell which one they were being shown — which is exactly how these
two metrics read "the reapers are dead" for hours on a host where the reaper units did not exist
to be asked.

`heartbeat_value` now gives every cap heartbeat **three outcomes**, following
`scripts/assert_volumes_in_service.py` (dcc3) where `UNKNOWN` stays distinct from
`NOT-IN-SERVICE` and both fail:

| value | means |
|---|---|
| `1` | in force |
| `0` | MEASURED and not in force |
| `-1` (`HEARTBEAT_UNKNOWN`) | the check could not be answered |

Applied to all five reads of this shape — the three alarmed heartbeats and the two unalarmed
quota facts, which share it.

**`bff5` is untouched, and deliberately so.** The distinction is carried in the VALUE, never by
withholding it: every heartbeat still publishes on every tick including its `0` path, so ABSENCE
remains reserved for "the publisher died". That reservation is what makes the dead-man
construction trustworthy under `treat_missing_data = "breaching"`, and spending it on "healthy
but unknown" would make every dead-man alarm on the box ambiguous to buy a local readability
win. Critically, **a measured `0` is still `0`** — only the previously-coerced case moves — so
every existing `bff5` expectation holds unchanged.

**Nothing is retuned and nothing pages differently.** All three alarms are
`LessThanThreshold 1.0`, so `-1` is below the threshold by construction. That is now
ENFORCED rather than asserted:
`test_observability_cap_deps.py::test_the_unknown_sentinel_still_breaches_every_alarm_on_that_heartbeat`
parses the real Terraform and fails if a comparison operator is flipped or a threshold drops to
`-1` or below — i.e. if someone silently converted "could not determine" into a non-event. No
Terraform was modified, so no apply is implicated.

The matching `rebar-health` log line now reads `could NOT determine ... <script> did not answer`
instead of `NOTHING is bounding /var/tmp`, so the log points at the probe's dependencies rather
than accusing the generator's ceiling. `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md` carries the
three-value table and what a `-1` means operationally.

New coverage: 5 parametrized cases pin `1` / `0` / `exit 127` / `exit 1` / empty-output to
`1` / `0` / `-1` / `-1` / `-1`. `make lint` and `make typecheck` clean; **158 tests** pass across
the affected `tests/scripts/` suites plus `tests/unit/test_alarm_window_tuning.py` (added
because this touches metrics that file governs).

**Remaining on this ticket:** only `octahedral-auburn-sunfish` — autodeploy's `*_PATHS` still do
not list the cap scripts, so a cap-only change reaches no host until something else
re-materializes the probe. That is an explicit non-goal here and is tracked there.

compiled_state.description:
## The defect

`infra/scripts/install-observability.sh:12` deploys ONLY the probe:

```
install -m 0755 "${SCRIPT_DIR}/observability.sh" /usr/local/bin/rebar-observability.sh
```

But `observability.sh` resolves its cap scripts as **siblings of its own path** — four of them,
not two (`:458` docker-storage-cap.sh, `:925` journald-cap.sh, `:999` vartmp-cap.sh,
`:1092` container-cap.sh), e.g.

```
DOCKER_CAP_SH="${DOCKER_CAP_SH:-$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/docker-storage-cap.sh}"
```

So the deployed probe at `/usr/local/bin/rebar-observability.sh` looks for all four in
`/usr/local/bin/`, where the installer never put any of them. The probe reports a value it cannot
actually measure, and the failure presents as a healthy-looking number.

## Consequences, both observed on the live host

**1. Gated percent metrics silently never publish.** `docker_storage_used_percent`,
`docker_buildkit_cache_used_percent`, `journal_used_percent`, `var_tmp_used_percent` and
`container_writable_used_percent` are each gated on a budget read from `--print-env`. With the
cap script unreachable the read fails, so the metric publishes NOTHING — correct
silence-not-zero behaviour firing for an incorrect reason. The caps were installed and readable
ON DISK, just not from where the probe looked.

**2. Ungated heartbeats are pinned at a FALSE 0 — the serious half.** These publish UNGATED, so
an unreachable cap script yields 0 rather than silence. `journal_cap_in_effect`,
`var_tmp_cleanup_active` and `container_reaper_active` assert "not in force" **forever, with the
mechanism genuinely in force on the host.** An alarm asserting a false negative indefinitely is
worse than a missing alarm: it trains its reader to ignore it, while the thing it watches is
healthy.

## How it was found

During an operator-authorised cap install on 2026-09-05. Installing both caps was NOT sufficient;
the scripts had to be placed at `/usr/local/bin/` by hand before `docker_storage_used_percent`
(63.0), `docker_buildkit_cache_used_percent` (100.0), `journal_used_percent` (56.0) appeared and
`journal_cap_in_effect` flipped 0 -> 1. `journald-cap.sh` did not exist on the host at all.
Adjacent to `octahedral-auburn-sunfish` (5246-2ec0-1fa6-4637): neither cap script appears in any
of `autodeploy.sh`'s `*_PATHS`, so a commit changing a cap signals nothing.

On 2026-09-06 the same defect was confirmed **still live** for `vartmp-cap.sh` and
`container-cap.sh` (rc 127 on both), and proven independent of host configuration: with both
reaper timers installed and genuinely running (`--check-active` = 1 at their installed paths),
the probe still published `0` for both heartbeats and still omitted both percentages on every
tick after the install. Evidence in the comment folding in `exorable-gemstone-bluefish`
(`1e63-bee1-5ce6-4d8f`, closed as a duplicate of this ticket).

## The constraint that shapes the fix

`docker-storage-cap.sh` and `journald-cap.sh` define no installed path, so their repo basename is
the only name they have and either fix direction works. **`vartmp-cap.sh` and `container-cap.sh`
self-install under a DIFFERENT name** (`VAR_TMP_INSTALLED_PATH` at `vartmp-cap.sh:121`,
`CONTAINER_INSTALLED_PATH` at `container-cap.sh:124`, both `/usr/local/bin/rebar-*-cap.sh`),
because that path is the `ExecStart` of the reaper units they write. Satisfying this by the
installer direction alone would place a SECOND copy under the unprefixed name — the probe reading
one copy while the reaper timer executes the other, free to drift. For those two the resolver
direction is the one that composes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 - A deployed probe can reach **every** cap script it resolves at runtime — all four.
      Either direction is acceptable per script; the invariant is that no `*_CAP_SH` default
      names a path nothing creates. Checked by AC4's deploy-time check.
- [ ] AC2 - Defect-seeded: with a cap script absent from the deploy location, a test FAILS.
      Removing it from the installer or from the resolver's candidate list must turn that test
      RED. Checked by `pytest tests/scripts/test_observability_docker_storage.py -x`.
- [ ] AC3 - Every ungated heartbeat distinguishes "not in force" from "could not determine".
      Publishing a confident 0 for an unreadable input is the defect. Covers
      `journal_cap_in_effect`, `var_tmp_cleanup_active` and `container_reaper_active`. Their
      alarms are `treat_missing_data = "breaching"` at 6/6, so silence still pages — it just
      stops asserting a false negative.
- [ ] AC4 - A check catches a deployed probe whose resolved dependencies are missing, so this is
      caught at deploy time rather than by an operator noticing absent metrics. Checked by the
      check failing when one cap script is withheld from a rendered install.
- [ ] AC5 - For `vartmp-cap.sh` / `container-cap.sh` exactly ONE copy of each remains on the
      host, at the `*_INSTALLED_PATH` their `--install` writes, and the probe resolves it. Test:
      with only `rebar-vartmp-cap.sh` beside the probe, a run publishes `var_tmp_used_percent`
      and `var_tmp_cleanup_active=1`; equivalently for the container pair.
- [ ] AC6 - The `*_CAP_SH` environment overrides still take precedence over every candidate, so
      existing tests injecting a stub path are unaffected.
- [ ] AC7 - `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass.

## Testing

- `pytest tests/scripts/test_observability_var_tmp.py tests/scripts/test_observability_container_layers.py -x`
- `pytest tests/scripts/test_observability_docker_storage.py tests/scripts/test_observability_journal.py -x`
- `pytest tests/scripts/test_vartmp_cap.py tests/scripts/test_container_cap.py -x`
- `make lint && make typecheck`
- Post-deploy: `aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace rebar/host --metric-name
  var_tmp_used_percent` returns datapoints and the two heartbeats read 1 on a reaper-active host.

## Non-goals

Not changing what the caps do. Not fixing the autodeploy `*_PATHS` gap
(`octahedral-auburn-sunfish`). Not restarting Docker. Not retuning any alarm: these alarms are
correct, and two are firing on conditions that are true.

file_impact.reason: Resolve all four *_CAP_SH defaults through an ordered candidate list including each script's *_INSTALLED_PATH; stop publishing a confident 0 for an unreadable heartbeat input.
Deploy the cap scripts the probe resolves, so a deployed probe can reach every dependency it names.
Installed-name layout regression case for var_tmp_used_percent and var_tmp_cleanup_active.
Installed-name layout regression case for container_writable_used_percent and container_reaper_active.
Defect-seeded case: a cap script absent from the deploy location must fail.
Same defect-seeded case for journald, plus journal_cap_in_effect silence-not-false-zero.

compiled_state.title: install-observability.sh deploys only the probe, so observability.sh cannot reach the cap scripts it resolves as siblings — three metrics stay silent and journal_cap_in_effect publishes a false 0 forever
